articles.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
articles.body:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Model Cards are intended to provide essential information on Gemini models, including known limitations, mitigation approaches, and safety performance. Model cards may be updated from time to time; for example, to include updated evaluations as the model is improved or revised.
Published: November 2026
Model Information
Description
Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows. While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are built for deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows.
Model dependencies
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon.
Inputs
Text strings (e.g., a question, a prompt, document(s) to be summarized), images, audio, and video files, with a combined input-output token context window of up to 1M.
Outputs
1M unified context window with up to 64K default synchronous output tokens / up to 1M via background long decode.
Architecture
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the model architecture for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Model Data
Training Dataset
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training dataset for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Training Data Processing
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training data processing for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Implementation and Sustainability
Hardware
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the hardware for Gemini 4 Hydrogen and our continued commitment to operate sustainably, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Software
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the software for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Distribution
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is distributed in the following channels; respective documentation shared in line:
Our models are available to downstream providers via an application program interface (API) and subject to relevant terms of use. There is no required hardware or software to use the model. For AI Studio and Gemini API, see the Gemini API Additional Terms of Service; for Gemini for business, see Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service. For more information, see Gemini Model API instructions, Gemini API quickstart, and Google Cloud documentation.
Evaluation
Approach
We evaluated Gemini 4 Hydrogen across a range of benchmarks, including agentic coding, knowledge work, computer use, multimodal understanding, science and math, and reasoning.
Additional benchmarks and details on approach, results and their methodologies can be found at: deepmind.com/models/evals-methodology/gemini-4-hydrogen.
Results
Gemini 4 Hydrogen results as of November, 2026 are below:
Intended Usage and Limitations
Benefit and Intended Usage
Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.
It is particularly well-suited for applications that require:
- fast, disciplined execution on its own or as sub-agents orchestrated alongside frontier models
- iterative repository coding and debugging
- open-ended agentic execution
- multimodal knowledge work
- web development
- adaptable speed and intelligence across four thinking levels
- ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work
- connecting the dots and getting more tasks done
- everyday prototyping and iteration
Known Limitations
Gemini 4 Hydrogen may exhibit some general limitations such as hallucinations. In addition to this, we are continually working to improve jailbreak resistance and have further strengthened mitigations across Frontier Safety. There may also be occasional slowness or timeout issues, and at times the model may use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher thinking levels. The knowledge cutoff for Gemini 4 Hydrogen is March 2026, though in some domains the model’s knowledge may be less up to date.
Acceptable Usage
Gemini 4 Hydrogen is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the acceptable usage for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Safety & Security
The full Safety & Security Report for Gemini 4 Hydrogen will be available in the coming days.
Evaluation Approach
For more information about the evaluation approach for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Safety Policies
For more information about the safety policies for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.
Training and Development Evaluation Results
Results for some of the internal safety evaluations conducted during the development phase are listed below. The evaluation results are for automated evaluations and not human evaluation or red teaming. Scores are provided as an absolute percentage increase or decrease in performance compared to the indicated model, as described below.
Overall, Gemini 4 Hydrogen outperforms Gemini 3.8 Flash on multimodal content safety, while text-to-text and multilingual safety remain at a similarly high safe response rate within confidence intervals. Refusal tone is similar to Gemini 3.8 Flash, while unjustified refusals are higher, particularly for multimodal prompts. We mark improvements in bolded green and regressions in red.
See the Gemini 4 Hydrogen Safety & Security Report (coming soon) for details.
We continue to improve our internal evaluations, including refining automated evaluations to reduce false positives and negatives, as well as update query sets to ensure balance and maintain a high standard of results. The performance results reported above are computed with improved evaluations and thus are not directly comparable with performance results found in previous Gemini model cards.
We expect variation in our automated safety evaluations results, which is why we review flagged content to check for egregious or dangerous material. Our manual review confirmed losses were overwhelmingly either a) false positives or b) not egregious.
Frontier Safety Assessment
We evaluated Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon in line with the Frontier Safety Framework (April 2026) and reported the results in the respective Safety and Security Reports (Argon, Carbon). Gemini 4 Hydrogen is part of the Gemini 4 series of models. We conducted a Material Capability Change (MCC) assessment to understand whether Gemini 4 Hydrogen has meaningful new capabilities or material increases in performance relative to the most recent model version subject to a critical capability assessment, which was Gemini 4 Argon. Gemini 4 Hydrogen did not show a material increase in general capability under our MCC assessment compared with Gemini 4 Argon and therefore a full suite of critical capability evaluations was not required in line with our FSF.
As we could not rule out that Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon reached the CBRN CCL for biological information risk and the Cybersecurity CCL, we conducted targeted critical capability assessments of Gemini 4 Hydrogen in the CBRN and cyber domains to understand the inherent risk of the model, and found that Gemini 4 Hydrogen does not reach the CBRN or cyber CCLs, though it reaches the CCL alert thresholds for both domains. A summary of our assessment is outlined in the table below, with full results in the Gemini 4 Hydrogen Safety & Security Report (coming soon).
Risks and Mitigations
Safety and security were built into Gemini 4 Hydrogen throughout the training and deployment lifecycle, including pre-training data filtering, post-training alignment (supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning), product- and system-level safety filtering, and usage monitoring. In addition, we strengthened Frontier Safety safeguards for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cybersecurity misuse. Key ongoing focus areas include resistance to adversarial jailbreaks and indirect prompt injections. For more information about the risks and mitigations, see the Gemini 4 Hydrogen Safety & Security Report (coming soon).

articles.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
articles.body:
I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang’s second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn’t he be? He’s placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he’s the only CEO Nvidia has ever had. L’état c’est moi.
The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.
The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.
Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out.
Why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained?
Fascinating. First of all, when I asked on Monday “Who else is Jensen Huang fucking?” I did not expect to get answers this fast — somebody, potentially somebody on the board (as we’ve seen in other incidents), wanted the story out there. Second, why throw Huang under the bus for getting his nuts drained? This is not an industry that cares about that kind of thing — just ask Eric Schmidt and Bill Gates. My guess is that the second affair is a pretext for action, and this all goes back to the original story from last week: that Huang was honeypotted by an alleged Chinese spy. Whatever was going on with neocloud Megaspeed might be much, much worse than we know, and what we know is pretty bad: business listings that led to “a Malaysian data center and shopping mall, a near-empty office in Singapore and a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur.”
Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46.
Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China. But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.”
Megaspeed was Nvidia’s largest Southeast Asian buyer, but Singaporean newspaper The Straits Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore office a month ago to find “no signs of activity.” Another building tenant told the reporters, “It is always dark for as long as it has been here. I hardly see anyone visiting or in the office.” The sole director of Megaspeed, Tan Yong Pong, appears to have vanished. The Singaporean company that owns Megaspeed, Swiftdata, has listed an office that belongs to an interior design firm as its business address.
Megaspeed is only part of the story
Incidentally, Alice Huang has surfaced in Beijing. The Financial Times says she’s barred from Singapore for giving police “inaccurate information.” Oh, and reportedly her companies invested in Chinese AI company DeepSeek and promised them Nvidia’s Blackwell chips? Fun!
Megaspeed is only part of the story, I think. There are two Chinese chip-related scandals that could cause serious problems for Nvidia, and both feature people with close ties to Huang. One is Megaspeed, which involves Huang’s maybe-spy affair partner. The other centers on Super Micro (which, horribly, does business as Supermicro), a partner of Nvidia run by one of Huang’s old friends, Charles Liang. Super Micro’s cofounder, Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, along with Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang and Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, allegedly defrauded the US by serving as a passthrough for a front company to buy $2.5 billion of Nvidia chips for Alibaba. The front company, not named in the indictment, is Thailand-based OBON, according to Bloomberg. Liang and Super Micro have not been charged.
But these incidents may not be the end of Nvidia’s problems. Take for instance, more recently, New Matrix — another company that barely exists, and yet is an approved buyer of Nvidia chips. It is, in fact, one of several approved companies that “have ties to firms that have been blacklisted by the U.S. government, or that work as military contractors in China,” according to The New York Times.
The question, of course, is how high this all goes
Huang has insisted that Nvidia has seen “no evidence of any AI chip diversion.” He’s been pretty emphatic on that point, actually. I am now wondering if that is even a little bit true. If the board is cutting Huang loose, there’s probably more on chip smuggling allegations coming.
More substantively, Nvidia reportedly intervened in a 2025 Commerce Department investigation of Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips — halting the investigation. Since the scandal broke, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appears to have become the fall guy for this, with Axios reporting that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent “confronted” him about failing to note Megaspeed as a national security concern and Politico saying “more than half a dozen Republicans have demanded answers” from him.
The question, of course, is how high this all goes. After all, Huang was awfully buddy-buddy with President Donald Trump, who was informed about Huang’s maybe-spy girlfriend in 2025 and apparently did nothing about it. Incidentally, Nvidia has reportedly donated $25 million to Trump’s planned ballroom. This is what gangster tech regulation looks like.
I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know?
Come January, Elizabeth Warren will be able to send subpoenas in her role as the chair of the Senate Banking Committee. And wouldn’t you know, she seems to be pretty interested. Democrats will control both the House and the Senate. Their voters have given them a mandate to root out corruption. And boy howdy, does Nvidia look like a sitting duck right now. If Huang knew chips were being diverted — or had reason to know that — and tried to ensure their sales anyway, he may have committed actual crimes (bribery, espionage, smuggling, whatever) and, under a functioning legal system, could actually go to jail. Nvidia dispensing with its indispensable CEO is the company reducing its risk of getting roped into Huang’s drama.
Will it be that easy for Nvidia? I wonder. The most interesting part of the second affair story, with Powell, the Nvidia vice president of healthcare, comes at the very end of the New York Times article. When someone took a video of Powell and Huang being “affectionate” in March, Huang’s security had nondisclosure agreements ready to go. CNBC reports that rumors of their affair have circulated “for years.” I wonder what else was an open secret at the company, you know? Especially since Huang had 60 direct reports, so every part of the company is covered in his fingerprints.
Over in the tech world, people still seem to be in denial. On X, the social network for Trumpist dead-enders, the account “zerohedge” posted, “Elon please hire Jensen.” Elon Musk replied, “That would be an honor.”

articles.title: US test reactor cleared for operations
articles.body:
The test reactor, near Lockhart in Caldwell County, Texas reached first criticality in August, less than a year after groundbreaking. It is one of 11 advanced reactor projects selected by the US Department of Energy (DOE) in August 2025 for the Nuclear Reactor Pilot Program, a programme aiming to expedite the testing of advanced reactor designs under a DOE authorisation pathway.
The DOE has now cleared the final operations hold point for the reactor - also known as Groves-1 - allowing the facility to advance into its research, testing, and training phase. This will help Oklo prepare the teams and systems needed to support the efficient delivery and operation of future nuclear projects, the company said. Operating experience from Groves-1 will directly inform Groves-2 Forge, Oklo's planned isotope production and processing pilot facility, which is part of the DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad initiative to promote the rapid development and implementation of advanced nuclear technologies by private industry.
With Groves-1 now cleared for unrestricted operations, Oklo said it will test its capabilities relevant to future isotope reactors and the company's fast fission reactor, the Aurora powerhouse.
Groves-1 will serve as a key training and qualification platform for nuclear personnel at future reactor deployments, alongside further equipment testing, including continued evaluations of control rod drive mechanism performance and reliability. It will also enable criticality and reactivity benchmarking operations that support Oklo's isotope production capabilities, its engineering and design models, and potentially light water reactors and the large light water reactor fleet. The company says the resulting data could also help improve fuel performance and power output in small and large light water reactors.
"Taking Groves-1 from greenfield to criticality in less than a year was an important demonstration of what our team can accomplish," Oklo CEO and co-founder Jacob DeWitte said. "Now we're building on that experience by operating the reactor, testing new capabilities, and learning directly from the work. Those lessons can help us develop the people, systems, and processes needed as we advance additional isotope projects and Aurora powerhouses."
"DOE's Reactor Pilot Program reset the nuclear industry's expectations for how quickly we can move from advanced reactor design to demonstration while upholding best-in-class safety standards," Acting Deputy Assistant Secretary for Nuclear Reactors Chimi Zacot said. "Successes like Groves-1's criticality are now paving the way for what comes next."
New reactor designs for commercial use in the USA are reviewed and approved by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), but under the Atomic Energy Act - the fundamental law governing civilian uses of nuclear materials and facilities in the USA - the DOE has the authority to approve reactor authorisations for research, development and demonstration. That authority is now being used to enable advanced reactor developers to certify, build and test prototype reactors that can inform full-scale commercial deployment under the Reactor Pilot Program pathway.
In response to executive orders issued in May 2025 that called for at least three prototype reactors to reach criticality by 4 July 2026, the DOE revamped its authorisation pathway to streamline the process.
In October, the NRC finalised a rule allowing applicants to use relevant analyses, test data and other information from DOE or Department of War (formerly the Department of Defense) reactor demonstration programmes to support commercial reactor licence applications. The rule is designed to make NRC reviews more efficient by allowing the agency to build on existing technical evidence while independently evaluating the safety of proposed commercial projects.

articles.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
articles.body:
Today, we're open-sourcing Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B, together with our unified inference framework and deployment tools. Edge0-145B is the world's first open-source on-device AI model with 145 billion parameters. It brings coding, reasoning, and agent capabilities that rival frontier cloud models to your own computer.
On-device AI has long forced a tradeoff between model capability and what the hardware can run. Larger models demand more memory, bandwidth, and power; smaller models can struggle with complex work. Moving that work to the cloud adds model-provider fees, data-handling constraints, and a dependence on connectivity.
This release addresses those constraints in four ways:
We're releasing the full stack so developers can reproduce the results, evaluate or fine-tune the models, and integrate them into their own products.
Get the model weights, explore the inference framework, or try the Edge0 App.
How We Make 100B+ Parameter AI Run on a Personal Computer
Edge0-145B Laptop Performance: Memory, Speed, and Power
Edge0-145B makes a 145-billion-parameter model usable on a personal laptop. A useful local model has to fit in memory, process prompts promptly, generate fast enough to use, and keep power consumption under control. It also needs to sustain longer tasks.
Our earlier Edge0-35B phone release reported peak memory below 2.5GB. On an iPhone 18 Pro Max, Edge0-35B delivers 37+ tokens/s using approximately 2.5GB of memory. Edge0-145B has roughly four times as many parameters; its laptop comparison reports 80+ tokens/s and 28GB peak memory. These measurements apply to different models and hardware.
On-device model scale over time. The chart covers 67 open models of at least 1B parameters from 14 labs, intended for phones, laptops, and AI PCs. Same-size base, instruct, and reasoning variants count once; each line tracks a lab's largest model, including releases before July 2025. Filled points mark new highs and hollow points other releases. The scale is logarithmic below 40B and linear above it. Apple is excluded because its weights are not released. Sources: vendor announcements and model cards.
Why On-Device Models Have Stayed Small
Memory limits kept most on-device models below 10B parameters before September 2026. Apple Intelligence's on-device foundation model had approximately 3B parameters, while Google's Gemini Nano came in 1.8B and 3.25B versions. Even a 7B model could consume approximately 4GB of memory.
Larger models faced a memory wall. Model weights occupy storage and must be read during generation, competing for limited memory and bandwidth with the operating system and other apps. Even an aggressively compressed 35B model could need approximately 20GB of memory, far more than a phone could make available.
Compute, bandwidth, and power created competing constraints. Larger models offered more capability, but strained memory capacity, generation speed, and battery life. Making models smaller helped them fit, often at the cost of capability.
Privacy alone could not close that gap. Apple Intelligence protected user data, but Apple acknowledged that its on-device model was not designed for agentic applications requiring general world knowledge. The prevailing assumption was that on-device intelligence could not match the cloud.
Under the Hood of Edge0: Four Layers of Model and Inference Design
We designed Edge0-145B and its inference engine together to reduce the memory and data movement that make large models difficult to run locally. The design spans architecture, training, loading, and scheduling.
Architecture: share large matrices across sparse experts. Sharing matrices substantially reduces the weights that must be stored and moved while keeping the expert count unchanged. Each group of 64 experts shares two large matrices, while each expert retains a small set of parameters that captures its differences. Previously, every expert stored a complete set of matrices. Of the model's 145B total parameters, only approximately 10B participate in computation on each inference step.
Training: build for local execution from day one. We train the model in its on-device architecture from the outset, with deployment constraints built into its design. This avoids treating local deployment as a compression or pruning step after training a cloud model.
Loading: pipeline GPU memory, system memory, and SSD access. Reading and computation overlap across three storage tiers, avoiding serial waits. Frequently used “hot experts” remain in GPU memory. An expert library of approximately 40GB sits in system memory, with experts brought into GPU memory as needed. Approximately 48GB of vocabulary data resides on the SSD and is read on demand.
Scheduling: use the CPU and GPU together. The GPU computes cached experts while the CPU handles the remaining work in parallel. Speculative decoding verifies multiple candidate tokens at once, spreading the cost of reading weights across more output tokens. These choices support the reported 80+ tokens/s decode rate.
Model and inference-engine design work together to make 100B+ parameter inference practical on personal computers. Source: internal testing.
Together, these changes let parameter counts grow from tens of billions to more than a hundred billion without proportional increases in memory use, power consumption, and latency.
What Edge0 Can Do: Anything From Chat to Complex Work on Your Computer
Edge0-145B can carry a complex task through to a usable result. Its coding and reasoning capabilities support local workflows that combine planning, tool use, execution, debugging, and visual checks. The benchmarks establish its capabilities; the demonstrations show how it puts them to work.
Coding and reasoning that rival frontier cloud models
Edge0-145B is competitive with specific frontier cloud models across coding, reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following:
- Coding: It scores 64.6 on DeepSWE 1.1, ahead of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next at 58.7 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at 54.4.
- Reasoning and knowledge: It scores 90.4 on GPQA-Diamond, close to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at 90.8 and Claude-Opus-4.6 \(Max\) at 91.3.
- Instruction following: It scores 80.6 on IFBench, ahead of DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at 79.2 and Claude-Opus-4.6 \(Max\) at 62.5.
Its 86.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 also exceeds Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 83.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's 82.7, and Claude's 78.2. On AA-LCR, Edge0-145B scores 79.3 to Claude's 78.0. These comparisons apply to the named models and evaluations.
Scores are percentages; higher is better. A dash means no public score is available, rather than a score of zero.
Edge0, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Claude results come from Edge0's internal evaluations. Claude-Opus-4.6 has no public DeepSWE 1.1 score. For Flint, Muse Glimmer, and Gemma 4, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and IFBench results come from the Recursive Flint evaluation; HLE, GPQA, and AA-LCR results come from Artificial Analysis.
The largest gains over Qwen3.8-27B, a mainstream on-device model baseline, are in agent and coding work: 18.5% on Terminal-Bench and 53.1% on DeepSWE. The relative gains on HLE, GPQA, and IFBench are 14.9%, 1.3%, and 1.4%, respectively.
DeepSWE 1.1 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 evaluate agent and coding work. HLE, GPQA-Diamond, and IFBench cover reasoning, knowledge, and instruction following. The complete evaluation setup, hardware environment, and reproduction instructions are being released with our technical report.
Competitive capability with a smaller memory footprint
Edge0-145B combines a 72.8 mean score across six benchmarks with 29GB measured peak memory. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next averages 71.7, with an estimated 70GB footprint for standard 4-bit deployment. That puts Edge0-145B at about 40% of the estimated baseline memory while delivering comparable or higher capability, enabling local use on a 48GB laptop.
The means cover DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal-Bench 2.1, HLE, GPQA-Diamond, IFBench, and AA-LCR. Edge0 memory figures are measured internal peaks. Asterisked baseline figures are estimates for standard 4-bit deployment and remain to be measured. Claude is excluded because it is cloud-only and has no DeepSWE score.
[Figure: Quality versus peak memory, with 48GB laptop and 64GB workstation capacities marked. Lower memory and higher scores are better; the chart's vertical axis does not start at zero.]
Local agents that plan, code, run, and check their work
A single natural-language request can start an entire local workflow. Edge0-145B breaks down the requirements, plans the steps, writes code, and calls tools to run it. When something fails, it debugs and repairs the code. It then takes screenshots to inspect the result and keeps iterating until the work is complete.
These projects often take dozens of rounds of planning, execution, and review. Local inference means those additional conversations, code revisions, and visual analyses incur no corresponding cloud-model token or API charges. Code and data can stay on the computer, and core model capabilities work offline.
Video production: generating Tesla's Roadster explainer within an hour
Edge0-145B produced an explainer about how Roadster could fly, handling technical research, scriptwriting, asset generation, and editing. We asked it to make the principles understandable to a general audience. The model ran locally without cloud-model calls or cloud token consumption, avoiding network round trips for inference.
The video was generated within an hour. Producing comparable work manually would have taken a director and scriptwriter, a 3D modeler, an editor, and a physics expert a month. An AI video workflow could previously cost more than hundreds of dollars; local inference eliminates the corresponding cloud-model token and API fees.
3D modeling: a Manhattan city scene in Blender
Edge0-145B built a 3D scene of Manhattan within an hour. Working in Blender from text and reference images, it constructed the scene, adjusted materials and lighting, and iterated on the rendered output.
The workflow brings visual inspection, code generation, and revision together inside Blender. The model works with objects, spatial relationships, and the creative goal, going beyond the pixels in a reference image. It inspects the result, writes code, and makes changes without handing those steps back to a person. The entire process stays local.
Creating a Manhattan-scale city scene manually would typically cost approximately $12,000-18,000 and take at least a month. A leading cloud model would still incur more than $150 in cloud token charges. Edge0-145B completes the local inference without those cloud-model token fees.
Game development: playable games and a medieval city
Edge0-145B can create playable games locally. We also used its 3D modeling capabilities to build an original medieval capital for a fantasy RPG and render a 20-second fly-through at game-trailer quality.
The model planned the city independently and built it from scratch in Blender: city walls, more than a thousand old-town homes, a plaza fountain, a Gothic twin-tower facade, a rib-vaulted nave, and stained-glass windows.
The fixed camera path made errors visible. Geometry clipping, occlusion, or incorrect proportions would appear along the route, so the model inspected the renders and corrected its work as it built. The workflow ran entirely locally.
A leading cloud model required hundreds of tool calls and hundreds of millions of tokens for a single completion, using the same prompt, reference images, and camera route. Edge0-145B delivered it on a laptop without cloud-model token or API fees for local inference. An art team would typically spend weeks and thousands of dollars producing a city scene to this standard.
Hardware control: code that flies a real drone
Edge0-145B wrote the program for a real drone from one instruction: “Write a drone program that navigates through obstacles and finds a red backpack.”
It generated the flight-control and visual-recognition programs locally. The drone then took off indoors, navigated through a dense row of obstacle poles, searched autonomously, and located the red backpack beside a wall. The task required no human-written code and no cloud call.
Hardware developers can describe the behavior they want and have the model turn it into a program for a real device, without moving repeatedly between an editor, documentation, and debugging tools.
PCB design: from KiCad layout to an assembly animation
Edge0-145B took a PCB design from component placement through an assembly visualization. We asked it to design a board for itself. It started from scratch in KiCad, placed components, routed a two-layer board, and imported the design into Unreal Engine 5. It then set up cameras and lighting and rendered an animation of PCB fabrication and assembly.
A single computer delivered work that previously required a hardware engineer and a 3D designer to hand tasks back and forth over several days. Schematics and board layouts can stay on the team's own hardware, supporting trade-secret protection and data-handling requirements without uploading the designs to a cloud model.
Why Edge0: A Full Stack for On-Device AI
Useful on-device AI requires model development, inference engineering, and hardware adaptation to work together. Our progress rests on three capabilities: developing complementary models quickly, optimizing the full stack, and carrying lessons from each deployment into the next.
Our September release of Edge0-35B showed what that approach could deliver on a phone. Its launch post passed 1.2 million views on its first day without paid promotion in overseas communities. Researchers and technical experts at OpenAI, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, and other companies shared it, and the model reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's overall Trending chart.
We released the model weights and unified inference framework together, giving companies and researchers a standard approach they could reproduce. The release helped move the discussion of on-device AI from a few billion parameters to the 35B tier.
Four Model Families for On-Device AI
Over the past year, we released 200 models across four families. Each handles a different part of the work, from listening and speaking to fast decisions, memory, and complex agent tasks.
The portfolio spans tens of millions to more than a hundred billion parameters. Both Edge0 and Audio8 have reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's Trending chart.
Models and Inference Systems Designed Together
We develop the model and the inference framework together, building hardware constraints into training and optimizing the engine for different chips. This connects model capability with the software and hardware needed to use it locally.
That work requires expertise in model development, inference frameworks, and low-level hardware adaptation. The combination is difficult for a company focused only on model development to reproduce.
Hardware Optimizations That Carry into Each Deployment
Each deployment gives us reusable optimizations for the next chip, model, or product. This matters because on-device hardware is fragmented: NPU architectures differ, as does support for numerical formats such as INT4, INT8, and FP4. A general-purpose model cannot automatically make full use of every chip.
We adapt to individual platforms. Our portfolio now covers 95% of mainstream chip platforms, including Qualcomm, BES, Rockchip, Allwinner, D-Robotics, and NVIDIA, across headphones, glasses, phones, PCs, and robots. This is portfolio-wide coverage; model requirements vary, and it does not mean every device can run Edge0-145B.
That deployment work now spans more than 5 million production devices. Our open-source models passed 15 million downloads within three months. By October 2026, we had more than 110,000 customer organizations.
The portfolio figures come from company papers and internal testing. They describe the broader Edge0 portfolio; the 145B performance results in this article apply specifically to Edge0-145B.
For Edge0-145B, day-one support covers macOS, Windows, and Linux, including Apple M-series chips and NVIDIA platforms such as RTX Spark, RTX 4090, and RTX 5090. The release includes one-click deployment tools and hardware guides.
The Future of On-Device AI and the Cloud
More complex work can stay on the device as local models approach cloud-level capability. Privacy, cost control, and offline access have long favored local execution; the remaining question was whether an on-device model could do the work. Edge0-145B expands the range of tasks for which it can.
Why More AI Work Can Stay Local
Local execution addresses four practical obstacles to adopting cloud-only AI:
- Control cloud-model costs. Local inference adds no corresponding cloud-model token or API fees as usage grows.
- Keep sensitive data local. Code, documents, and business records can stay on the hardware, giving teams control over data handling.
- Sustain a responsive experience. Model and inference-engine design address response speed, power use, system responsiveness, and continuous operation together.
- Keep core capabilities available offline. Local tasks continue when connectivity drops; features that depend on online information or services still need a connection.
From Cloud First to More Complex Work On-Device
We see the division of work between devices and the cloud shifting through three stages.
Before September 2026: cloud first, with on-device support. Apple Intelligence reflected this stage: it protected privacy, but handled a limited range of tasks locally while more demanding work relied on cloud capabilities.
After Edge0-35B's September 10 release: everyday tasks locally, complex tasks in the cloud. Local models could take on frequent requests that needed immediate responses. For one leading headphone manufacturer, our hybrid solution now handles 92% of AI usage on-device and 8% in the cloud. Everyday conversation accounts for most use cases on consumer wearables.
With Edge0-145B: toward on-device first, with cloud support. Vibe coding and other complex tasks can now run on a personal computer, giving teams more scope to choose local execution. This extends the range of work that can stay on the device while preserving the cloud for tasks and hardware that need it.
The diagram shows the shift from cloud-first AI to everyday local tasks and then more complex local work. Its colored areas are schematic, not measured usage shares.
Where Cloud AI Still Fits
Hardware constraints still determine which model fits. Compute capacity, heat, and battery life matter: Edge0-35B runs on phones, while Edge0-145B runs on suitably equipped laptops. A very low-compute device cannot currently run a 145B model locally. It needs a smaller model suited to its hardware or cloud access to a model of that size.
Cross-device long-term memory and searches requiring highly current information still require cloud services. Local and cloud models can work together; the appropriate split depends on the task, the hardware, and the information it needs.
The aim is to make local execution a practical choice for demanding work, with a capable model that can keep working close to the person using it. That is the next step toward our goal of enabling intelligence at zero distance for everybody.
Get Started with Edge0
Download the models to run locally, evaluate or fine-tune them, and build them into your own products:
- Model weights: Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B on Hugging Face.
- Inference framework and deployment guides: Edge0 on GitHub.
- Try it without environment setup: Download the Edge0 App. Its core model capabilities work offline, without an account or usage quota.
- Community: Join us on Discord.
For hardware or product integrations, reach the Edge0 team through GitHub or contact@autoark.ai.

It then set up cameras and lighting and rendered an animation of PCB fabrication and assembly.
A single computer delivered work that previously required a hardware engineer and a 3D designer to hand tasks back and forth over several days. Schematics and board layouts can stay on the team's own hardware, supporting trade-secret protection and data-handling requirements without uploading the designs to a cloud model.
Why Edge0: A Full Stack for On-Device AI
Useful on-device AI requires model development, inference engineering, and hardware adaptation to work together. Our progress rests on three capabilities: developing complementary models quickly, optimizing the full stack, and carrying lessons from each deployment into the next.
Our September release of Edge0-35B showed what that approach could deliver on a phone. Its launch post passed 1.2 million views on its first day without paid promotion in overseas communities. Researchers and technical experts at OpenAI, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, and other companies shared it, and the model reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's overall Trending chart.
We released the model weights and unified inference framework together, giving companies and researchers a standard approach they could reproduce. The release helped move the discussion of on-device AI from a few billion parameters to the 35B tier.
Four Model Families for On-Device AI
Over the past year, we released 200 models across four families. Each handles a different part of the work, from listening and speaking to fast decisions, memory, and complex agent tasks.
The portfolio spans tens of millions to more than a hundred billion parameters. Both Edge0 and Audio8 have reached No. 1 on Hugging Face's Trending chart.
Models and Inference Systems Designed Together
We develop the model and the inference framework together, building hardware constraints into training and optimizing the engine for different chips. This connects model capability with the software and hardware needed to use it locally.
That work requires expertise in model development, inference frameworks, and low-level hardware adaptation. The combination is difficult for a company focused only on model development to reproduce.
Hardware Optimizations That Carry into Each Deployment
Each deployment gives us reusable optimizations for the next chip, model, or product. This matters because on-device hardware is fragmented: NPU architectures differ, as does support for numerical formats such as INT4, INT8, and FP4. A general-purpose model cannot automatically make full use of every chip.
We adapt to individual platforms. Our portfolio now covers 95% of mainstream chip platforms, including Qualcomm, BES, Rockchip, Allwinner, D-Robotics, and NVIDIA, across headphones, glasses, phones, PCs, and robots. This is portfolio-wide coverage; model requirements vary, and it does not mean every device can run Edge0-145B.
That deployment work now spans more than 5 million production devices. Our open-source models passed 15 million downloads within three months. By October 2026, we had more than 110,000 customer organizations.
The portfolio figures come from company papers and internal testing. They describe the broader Edge0 portfolio; the 145B performance results in this article apply specifically to Edge0-145B.
For Edge0-145B, day-one support covers macOS, Windows, and Linux, including Apple M-series chips and NVIDIA platforms such as RTX Spark, RTX 4090, and RTX 5090. The release includes one-click deployment tools and hardware guides.
The Future of On-Device AI and the Cloud
More complex work can stay on the device as local models approach cloud-level capability. Privacy, cost control, and offline access have long favored local execution; the remaining question was whether an on-device model could do the work. Edge0-145B expands the range of tasks for which it can.
Why More AI Work Can Stay Local
Local execution addresses four practical obstacles to adopting cloud-only AI:
- Control cloud-model costs. Local inference adds no corresponding cloud-model token or API fees as usage grows.
- Keep sensitive data local. Code, documents, and business records can stay on the hardware, giving teams control over data handling.
- Sustain a responsive experience. Model and inference-engine design address response speed, power use, system responsiveness, and continuous operation together.
- Keep core capabilities available offline. Local tasks continue when connectivity drops; features that depend on online information or services still need a connection.
From Cloud First to More Complex Work On-Device
We see the division of work between devices and the cloud shifting through three stages.
Before September 2026: cloud first, with on-device support. Apple Intelligence reflected this stage: it protected privacy, but handled a limited range of tasks locally while more demanding work relied on cloud capabilities.
After Edge0-35B's September 10 release: everyday tasks locally, complex tasks in the cloud. Local models could take on frequent requests that needed immediate responses. For one leading headphone manufacturer, our hybrid solution now handles 92% of AI usage on-device and 8% in the cloud. Everyday conversation accounts for most use cases on consumer wearables.
With Edge0-145B: toward on-device first, with cloud support. Vibe coding and other complex tasks can now run on a personal computer, giving teams more scope to choose local execution. This extends the range of work that can stay on the device while preserving the cloud for tasks and hardware that need it.
The diagram shows the shift from cloud-first AI to everyday local tasks and then more complex local work. Its colored areas are schematic, not measured usage shares.
Where Cloud AI Still Fits
Hardware constraints still determine which model fits. Compute capacity, heat, and battery life matter: Edge0-35B runs on phones, while Edge0-145B runs on suitably equipped laptops. A very low-compute device cannot currently run a 145B model locally. It needs a smaller model suited to its hardware or cloud access to a model of that size.
Cross-device long-term memory and searches requiring highly current information still require cloud services. Local and cloud models can work together; the appropriate split depends on the task, the hardware, and the information it needs.
The aim is to make local execution a practical choice for demanding work, with a capable model that can keep working close to the person using it. That is the next step toward our goal of enabling intelligence at zero distance for everybody.
Get Started with Edge0
Download the models to run locally, evaluate or fine-tune them, and build them into your own products:
- Model weights: Edge0-145B and Edge0-120B on Hugging Face.
- Inference framework and deployment guides: Edge0 on GitHub.
- Try it without environment setup: Download the Edge0 App. Its core model capabilities work offline, without an account or usage quota.
- Community: Join us on Discord.
For hardware or product integrations, reach the Edge0 team through GitHub or contact@autoark.ai.

articles.title: Microsoft says attempts to fix global outage not going 'as expected'
articles.body:
NHS England says the outage is "inevitably" disrupting staff but appointments can continue; schools ask parents to get in touch via phone not email; US federal government and court systems are also reporting issues

0:31The impact of the outage in the Asia-Pacific region. 00:00:31, play videoThe impact of the outage in the Asia-Pacific region
1:24'I feel it's a sign of what's to come': Office workers say. 00:01:24, play video'I feel it's a sign of what's to come': Office workers say

Live Reporting
Edited by Jamie Whitehead and Manish Pandey, with technology reporters Tom Gerken, Shiona McCallum and Laura Cress
'If the emails weren’t going to go back on, it was time to go to the pub'published at 15:47 GMT
15:47 GMT
Nick Johnson Reporting from London
The Golden Goose pub is tucked inside Leadenhall Market in
the heart of the City of London.
While many of the customers joked with me earlier that they
would “be here at this time on a Friday anyway,” one group of drinkers
confessed they would have been in the office had it not been for the Microsoft outage.
This group of five work in banking and told me they’d
arrived at work as normal today, but had “given up” by late-morning as
the email system was down.
“Everyone in the office decided that at around 11:00, if the
emails weren’t going to go back on, it was time to go to the pub,” Pippy Isaacs
tells me.
Microsoft outage is 'prime time' for scammers, cyber expert warnspublished at 15:33 GMT
15:33 GMT
Shiona McCallum Senior technology reporter
Image source, Getty images
Cyber security expert Ken Munro warns businesses and
individuals who have been switching to messaging apps during the Microsoft
outage could potentially put personal data at risk.
"If email is down, many will move to WhatsApp and other
platforms, so there's a risk to sensitive data being shared on less secure
platforms," he says.
Munro says email outages and cyber events like this are
"a prime time for scammers".
He warns fake support messages about the outage could be
used to "extract passwords from people and install malware".
The warning, as ever, during these cyber security incidents
is to be careful of clicking on links and pause if something doesn't look
right.
Microsoft shares open flat as traders brush off outagepublished at 15:15 GMT
15:15 GMT
Mitchell Labiak Business reporter
Image source, Reuters
Shares in Microsoft dipped 0.2% in early trading in the US,
suggesting that investors are not all that worried about what the outage could
mean for the tech giant.
It seems remarkable considering the immense amount of disruption the outage has
caused around the world, but share price movements depend on earnings
predictions, not public sentiment.
As such, for Microsoft investors, there are only two big questions today: Will
the firm be liable for compensation as a result of this issue? And will its
customers cancel their subscriptions to its services en masse in response?
The share price movement, or lack thereof, implies that the majority of traders
believe the answer to both of those questions is "no".
Delays cause stress at Westminster Magistrates' Courtpublished at 15:03 GMT
15:03 GMT
Ewan Somerville Reporting from Westminster Magistrates' Court
The Microsoft outage has had a knock-on effect at some
courts across the country - including here at Westminster Magistrates' Court.
A member of court staff told me they had experienced "a
lot of delays as the whole system has been down".
"It's been stressful," she says. "Judges have
been unable to access systems, the prosecution hasn't been able to send papers
through, and we've been unable to get pre-sentence reports."
I saw huddles of defendants and their legal teams
waiting for each courtroom to become available.
But it was orderly and did not feel chaotic. As I left early
on Friday afternoon, some of the court's systems were coming back online and
staff were working to catch up on dozens of listings for extradition cases and
others.
A Ministry of Justice source told me: "Courts are still
operating, and we have contingencies in place, obviously everything is a bit
clunky as we look to manage the situation."
Communication with Europe has 'come to a standstill,' says South African winemakerpublished at 14:41 GMT
14:41 GMT
Alex Akhurst Your Voice
Image source, Peter Pentz
A winemaker in South Africa says almost his entire business
has been brought to a "standstill" by the Microsoft outage.
"It's incredibly frustrating. We export a lot, so
communication with exporters in Europe has come to a standstill," says
Peter Pentz.
He says order processing, dispatch, communications and even
"critical production work" has been halted, as the Cape West Coast
winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day
operations".
Pentz adds that "with the festive season coming, it's
really bad timing".
"It's quite ironic that we're so advanced in AI and
automation and stuff, and yet something as simple as Outlook not working can
have such an impact," he adds.
"What’s striking is how quickly a single technology
outage can interrupt several parts of a business at once."
Outage affecting hospitals, rail passengers and universities in Canadapublished at 14:29 GMT
14:29 GMT
Nadine Yousif Reporting from Toronto
Image source, Getty Images
Image caption,
St Michael's Hospital, part of Toronto's Unity Health Network.
Like its neighbour the United States, many of Canada's
institutions appear to be heavily reliant on Microsoft for their email and
online communication needs.
A hospital network in Toronto has declared a "Code
Grey" because of the outage, which is activated in the event of
"infrastructure failure".
In a statement on its website, Unity Health Toronto says
its teams are experiencing difficulties sending and receiving emails and is urging
patients to call via the main hospital phone line instead.
It adds that patient care is not affected and the hospitals
"remain safe and open".
The outage has also hit Via Rail, Canada's national railway
network. In a post on X, Via Rail says its passengers may not be able to
receive information about their trip via email and is asking them to sign up to
updates via text message instead.
The cites of Ottawa and Vancouver are also reporting
disruptions, as are some of the country’s universities.
Cop31 attendees struggling to access negotiating documents as outage affects Turkey conferencepublished at 14:16 GMT
14:16 GMT
Image source, Reuters
Image caption,
Some delegates are using WhatsApp to communicate, which is not affected
Advisors and officials attending the United Nations Climate
Change Conference, Cop31, in Antalya, Turkey have been left frustrated by the
Outlook outage.
James Young works as a climate change advisor at the Inuit
Circumpolar Council, the organisation which represents around 180,000 Inuit
people living in the Arctic.
He tells the Reuters news agency the council relies on
emails and Microsoft Teams to communicate across several countries.
"It's just been really frustrating and challenging to
maintain contact with our colleagues and to be able to effectively participate
here," he adds.
“I think our dependence on technology leaves us vulnerable
to situations like this.”
Anna Hopper Schulz, another climate advisor at COP31,
explains it has been "really difficult to access negotiating documents and
share updates".
"Fortunately, WhatsApp hasn't been that affected. I
think we're more dependent on WhatsApp than we are on Microsoft, but it still
has made it very difficult to open and share negotiating documents,” she adds.
Microsoft says it is continuing to see improvementspublished at 14:05 GMT
14:05 GMTBreaking
Microsoft says it is continuing "to see improvements in
service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching
normal levels".
In its latest update it says some users "may still
experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery
continues".
It says it has brought in further measures and is
"restoring the remaining affected infrastructure while investigating
residual service issues".
"We're closely monitoring service health and validating
recovery across affected connection methods to ensure sustained service
stability.
"At this time, we have no evidence of malicious
activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with
urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full Post-Incident Report
with root cause and defence-in-depth actions after mitigation is
complete," the update adds.
Indian software company an unlikely star for some firmspublished at 13:50 GMT
13:50 GMT
Soutik Biswas India Correspondent, in Delhi
Image source, Getty Images
Microsoft’s global outage has unexpectedly drawn attention
to Indian software company Zoho, with some users taking to social media to say
their work has continued uninterrupted because they use its workplace tools
instead of Microsoft’s.
The company, which offers a suite of business applications
as an alternative to products such as Microsoft 365, has become an unlikely
talking point as users discuss their dependence on overseas technology
platforms.
Some posts have presented the disruption as an opportunity
for Indian software alternatives, although there is little evidence yet of a
significant shift in users or businesses.
Zoho has not publicly commented on the outage. The episode
has nevertheless offered the company an unusual moment of visibility amid
questions about the resilience of workplace technology.
Why has it taken Microsoft so long to fix the outage?published at 13:27 GMT
13:27 GMT
Laura Cress Technology reporter
Image source, EPA
This has now lasted more than 20 hours, which in outage
terms makes it very long lasting.
Though email service Outlook does appear to be returning,
for some at least, the question remains: why has this disruption taken so long
to fix?
Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading says what
Microsoft has disclosed gives us some clues.
He points out that it has reported that servers which set up
secure connections have been getting "swamped" - and then the server
"just stops answering".
"The trouble is that this kind of failure
snowballs," he says.
"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the
next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get
back in."
"You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have
to bring it back bit by bit."
The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault but
managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start
coming back online.
'Improvements' in North America and Europe, Microsoft says in latest updatepublished at 13:15 GMT
13:15 GMTBreaking
In its latest update, Microsoft says there is
"continued recovery progress across affected regions, with broader
improvements now observed in North America and sustained improvements
across much of Europe".
"We're also seeing encouraging recovery signals in Asia
Pacific," Microsoft says, but adds that some users may continue to
experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery.
Government and court services slowed across the US as outage continuespublished at 13:07 GMT
13:07 GMT
Madeline Halpert Reporting from New York
We’re getting a sense of how the outage is affecting the US.
Local municipalities, the federal government and court
systems are some of the many entities that have reported issues.
Baltimore County Government says employees are "currently unable to send
or receive emails due to the widespread Microsoft outage. 911 and other
essential County services are NOT affected”.
Government officials in Austin, Texas said the same, also stressing emergency services were still active.
Staff with the US House of Representatives told reporters their work had been
halted by the outage.
“We all use Outlook, that’s our life, everything is there, our calendar is
there, our boss’s calendar, so it has been a challenge,” one House staff member
told Politco. “There goes a day of legislative work.”
Courts across the US had to pause some work. New York’s Department of
Investigation told city marshals to suspend evictions scheduled for Friday
because the outage affected systems and applications.
Colorado’s judicial branch said the outage has “impacted court operations”.
“We are currently not able to send or receive emails or
access other Microsoft programs,” the court said.
Outage becoming a punchline for some office workers in Indiapublished at 12:49 GMT
12:49 GMT
Soutik Biswas India Correspondent, in Delhi
Microsoft’s global outage has prompted some wry reactions
from Indian users, with Reddit turning into a running commentary on workplace
disruption.
In a thread titled “Outlook and Teams are down, is it early
weekend?” one user joked in Hindi that employees would now have to make up for
the lost work on Saturday.
Another user described going to their workplace’s IT
department to report a laptop battery problem, only to find someone else
already there asking the technician to fix Outlook.
The exchange captured the peculiar comedy of a workplace
where even routine IT complaints have been pushed aside by a global technology
outage.
Microsoft outage not on everyone’s radar in the Middle Eastpublished at 12:36 GMT
12:36 GMT
Ethar Shalaby BBC News Arabic
Image source, Getty Images
Image caption,
Many supermarkets in the Middle East rely on WhatsApp for customer orders, which is not affected
I have been speaking over the phone with people the Middle
East and North Africa to see how they are being impacted by the Microsoft outage.
Some say their work remains unaffected, but others are
bracing for potential disruption.
Karim Belhajj, a taxi driver in Tunisia, said he was unaware
of the outage and didn’t expect it to affect his work unless ride-hailing apps
were disrupted.
In Egypt, teacher Nadia Abduallah says her private tuition
sessions are continuing as normal, as she relies on Zoom and Google Meet.
But another teacher expects disruption when schools resume
on Sunday if the outage persists, saying her school relies heavily on
Microsoft's OneDrive.
“This will be a problem for me when I go to work on Sunday
because that is where we store all the school files,” Yosra Abdel Hai says.
Omneya Farid works in the banking sector and says she had
not heard about the outage, suggesting employees would be informed internally
if the disruption affects their work.
Meanwhile, calls to a number of supermarkets across the Middle
East revealed how far removed some businesses are from the disruption.
Staff gave bemused responses when asked about Outlook and
even Microsoft, with some saying they were only concerned about WhatsApp, which
they rely on to receive customer orders.
Encouraging recovery progress in Europe, Microsoft sayspublished at 12:22 GMT
12:22 GMT
We've had another update from Microsoft detailing recovery
in various regions.
The company says it is now seeing "encouraging recovery
progress in Europe", with service availability and email delivery
performance "improving across a growing portion" of infrastructure.
"Japan remains comparatively more stable, while North
America is also improving; however, some users may still experience
intermittent issues as recovery actions continue," the online statement
says.
The company says it is focussed on "addressing the
remaining areas of disruption".
Some companies delay announcing quarterly resultspublished at 12:12 GMT
12:12 GMT
Archana Shukla Reporting from Singapore
Some companies reporting quarterly financial results today
are delaying their announcements.
The Swiss luxury goods group, Richemont, that owns brands
like Cartier and Chloé, said its half-year numbers will be delayed owing to the
Microsoft service disruption.
US electric truck maker Workhorse Group has also moved its
quarterly report to next week.
Vital services disrupted as Microsoft outage still not fixed - a recappublished at 11:58 GMT
11:58 GMT
Freya Scott-Turner Live reporter
Image source, Getty Images
Friday has been thrown into disarray for tens of thousands globally. The problem: a massive outage affecting multiple Microsoft services. Let's get up to speed:
What's going on?
Multiple Microsoft tools - including Teams, Outlook, Copilot and OneDrive - were hit with "connectivity problems" on Thursday, leaving many people unable to access them
Microsoft stated that the cause was an overloading of some of its servers, after other ones had become "unexpectedly unavailable"
There's seemingly been no quick fix. More than 16 hours later, Microsoft says it's seeing "early signs" of systems stabilising, but says capacity has "not yet returned to normal levels"
The impact has been huge
Microsoft hasn't disclosed exactly how many people are affected, but about 430 million people use its tools. Tens of thousands across more than 70 countries have reported issues on Downdetector - but this is likely to be a vast underestimate
It's "very rare" for an issue affecting this many people to take so long to be fixed, which could make it the "most disruptive" business email outage of all time, our technology report hears
This incident highlights the risks faced by businesses that rely on a single technology provider for major operation needs, writes our Asia business producer
Outage affects couple's first house purchasepublished at 11:45 GMT
11:45 GMT
Georgia from Staffordshire says she was due to complete her first house purchase today, after waiting eight months to get to this point - but it has been delayed due to the outage.
"The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies. We’re not the only one completing today, there are 100s of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible," Georgia says.
Banks and estate agencies have told the BBC they are having issues due to the outage.
Housing author and journalist Peter Bill says: "Friday tends to be the day of completion for many sales, with 4pm being the deadline for the funds to be transferred, allowing the keys to be released to the buyer.
"A single delay can break a whole chain of transactions. There will be a lot of heads being banged into a lot of walls today."
